lines.text: Can one day outlast a year? On Venus: yes. And no.
lines.phonemes: kæn wˈʌn dˈeɪ aʊtlˈæst ɐ jˈɪɹ? ˌɔn vˈiːnəs: jˈɛs. ænd nˈoʊ.

lines.text: On Earth, you see the Sun rise about three hundred sixty-five times a lap. Next door, Venus hides its face under a permanent lid of cloud.
lines.phonemes: ˌɔn ˈɜːθ, juː sˈiː ðə sˈʌn ɹˈaɪz ɐbˌaʊt θɹˈiː hˈʌndɹɪd sˈɪkstifˈaɪv tˈaɪmz ɐ lˈæp. nˈɛkst dˈɔːɹ, vˈiːnəs hˈaɪdz ɪts fˈeɪs ˌʌndɚɹ ɐ pˈɜːmənənt lˈɪd ʌv klˈaʊd.

lines.text: For three hundred years, astronomers chased faint smudges in those clouds. The Cassinis, father and son, clocked about twenty-three hours. Schiaparelli said one face always faced the Sun.
lines.phonemes: fɔːɹ θɹˈiː hˈʌndɹɪd jˈɪɹz, ɐstɹˈɑːnəmɚz tʃˈeɪst fˈeɪnt smˈʌdʒᵻz ɪn ðoʊz klˈaʊdz. ðə kəsˈiːniz , fˈɑːðɚɹ ænd sˈʌn, klˈɑːkt ɐbˌaʊt twˈɛntiθɹˈiː ˈaʊɚz. skjˌɑːpəɹˈɛli sˈɛd wˈʌn fˈeɪs ˈɔːlweɪz fˈeɪsd ðə sˈʌn.

lines.text: In nineteen sixty-two, radar from a dish in California pierced the clouds. Both guesses were wrong. Venus turns once every two hundred forty-three days, longer than its year. And it turns backwards.
lines.phonemes: ɪn nˈaɪntiːn sˈɪkstitˈuː, ɹˈeɪdɑːɹ fɹʌm ɐ dˈɪʃ ɪn kˌælɪfˈɔːɹniə pˈɪɹst ðə klˈaʊdz. bˈoʊθ ɡˈɛsᵻz wɜː ɹˈɔŋ. vˈiːnəs tˈɜːnz wˈʌns ˈɛvɹi tˈuː hˈʌndɹɪd fˈɔːɹɾiθɹˈiː dˈeɪz, lˈɔŋɡɚ ðɐn ɪts jˈɪɹ. ænd ɪt tˈɜːnz bˈækwɚdz.

lines.text: Stand there, and the spin and the orbit team up. The Sun comes back every hundred and seventeen days, rising in the west.
lines.phonemes: stˈænd ðˈɛɹ, ænd ðə spˈɪn ænd ðɪ ˈɔːɹbɪt tˈiːm ˈʌp. ðə sˈʌn kˈʌmz bˈæk ˈɛvɹi hˈʌndɹɪd ænd sˈɛvəntˌiːn dˈeɪz, ɹˈaɪzɪŋ ɪnðə wˈɛst.

lines.text: So yes: one turn outlasts a year. But the day you'd live by is the Sun coming back.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ jˈɛs: wˈʌn tˈɜːn aʊtlˈæsts ɐ jˈɪɹ. bˌʌt ðə dˈeɪ juːd lˈaɪv baɪ ɪz ðə sˈʌn kˈʌmɪŋ bˈæk.

lines.text: Light time, Sun to Venus: six minutes. The radar's round trip, at its closest: about four minutes.
lines.phonemes: lˈaɪt tˈaɪm, sˈʌn tə vˈiːnəs: sˈɪks mˈɪnɪts. ðə ɹˈeɪdɑːɹz ɹˈaʊnd tɹˈɪp, æɾ ɪts klˈoʊsɪst: ɐbˌaʊt fˈɔːɹ mˈɪnɪts.

lines.text: Next: the Moon never stops falling toward us. So why doesn't it land?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: ðə mˈuːn nˈɛvɚ stˈɑːps fˈɔːlɪŋ təwˈɔːɹd ˌʌs. sˌoʊ wˌaɪ dˈʌzənt ɪt lˈænd?
